project.name: Notes Vault
project.idea: A private notes API: each user creates, lists, reads and deletes only their own notes.

phases.name: Core API
phases.goal: Implement the notes API, file persistence, security controls and the full test suite per design rev 2
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: POST /notes returns 201 and the full note per schema; title 1-100 after trim, body max 2000
AC2: GET /notes returns only the caller's notes, newest first
AC3: GET /notes/:id returns the note only to its owner; 404 for others, unknown and non-UUID ids
AC4: DELETE /notes/:id returns 204 only for the owner; otherwise 404 and nothing deleted
AC5: all errors follow the {error:{code,message}} contract (400, 404, 405 with Allow, 415, 422, fixed 500) with no stack or path leaks
AC6: X-User strictly validated (regex, duplicate header, comma) giving 401 before body parsing; __proto__ works as an isolated user
AC7: body over 16 KB gives 413 and the connection closes; 501st note gives 409 note_limit_reached; delete re-allows create

AC8: notes and deletions survive restart; leftover .tmp or corrupt data file makes the service refuse to start (exit 1, stderr message) and the file is never overwritten; atomic temp+rename writes; file mode 0600
AC9: default bind 127.0.0.1; HOST/PORT env override; non-loopback HOST logs the trusted-gateway startup warning
AC10: one log line per request (method, route template, status, duration); sentinel title/body never appears in logs
AC11: automated tests cover AC1-AC10 per the design's AC traceability matrix, and NFR3 perf check (p95 < 50 ms) passes; all required test files exist

api.title: Implement notes API, file persistence, security controls and tests
inputs: .eccode/artifacts/design.md (Components, Interface Contracts, Data Design, Security, Testing Strategy, AC-to-test traceability matrix, Implementation Workflow)
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: create returns 201 with full schema note (api.test.js)
AC2: list is owner-only, newest first, tie-break by insertion (api.test.js)
AC3: non-owner/unknown/non-UUID GET gives identical 404 (security.test.js)
AC4: non-owner DELETE gives 404 and deletes nothing; owner gets 204 (security.test.js)
AC5: error contract and forced-500 no-leak test (api.test.js)
AC6: X-User validation table, duplicate header, __proto__/constructor isolation (security.test.js)
AC7: 16 KB cap with 413 and connection close, 500-note cap with 409 (limits.test.js)
AC8: restart persistence, leftover .tmp and corrupt file refuse to start with file unchanged, failed flush rollback, mode 0600 (persistence.test.js, file-repository.test.js)
AC9: default 127.0.0.1, HOST/PORT overrides, non-loopback warning on stderr (security.test.js)
AC10: sentinel title/body absent from logs, one line per request with route template (logging.test.js)
AC11: every test file in the design traceability matrix exists and passes; perf.js p95 < 50 ms (NFR3)

verification.method: Run the full suite and perf check per design Testing Strategy; first confirm all required test files exist (api, security, limits, persistence, logging, validate, identity, file-repository, perf) so a missing file fails CI; results map to the AC traceability matrix. Order of work: Follow the design's Implementation Workflow in order: (1) config, errors, identity, validate + unit tests; (2) FileNoteRepository + persistence tests, body reader, logger; (3) service, app, server + integration, security, limits and logging tests; (4) perf.js and README (single instance, gateway/X-User trust, DATA_FILE, HOST/PORT, backup, rollback). Zero runtime dependencies. Satisfy the design's AC-to-test traceability matrix; every AC1-AC11 must have its named test file/cases.
verification.command: for f in api security limits persistence logging validate identity file-repository; do test -f test/$f.test.js || { echo missing test/$f.test.js; exit 1; }; done && test -f test/perf.js && node --test test/ && node test/perf.js

rev-muzjb5ui-01c5a2e0.summary: Brief is clear on core CRUD and privacy, but the in-memory store contradicts the stated problem, and abuse/resource limits, identity validation and the risk register are incomplete.

criteria.description: Not met: no limits on request size, notes per user or memory; X-User format unspecified; no logging; no id scheme.
Not met: AC5 'clear message' and 'never causes a server error' are vague; no AC for oversized bodies, wrong types; check order of 401 vs 400/422 undefined.
Not met: A1 is unverifiable by the service and mitigated only by a README sentence.
Met: zero-dependency node:http plus repository interface is proportionate.
Met: straightforward with node:http.
Not met: spoofable identity header, no body size cap, unbounded memory growth (DoS).
Met: no AI features; not applicable.
Not met: only two risks; no likelihood, impact or owner; DoS and gateway-misconfiguration spoofing not listed.

findings.title: In-memory store does not solve the stated problem
findings.detail: Problem says local files are 'lost between machines' and need an API; but RISK-2/Q1 accept data loss on every restart, so the product is not a reliable private notes place. Persistence is deferred with no date (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Problem, #Risks, #Open Questions).
findings.recommendation: Either add file/DB persistence behind the repository interface to scope, or explicitly redefine this release as a prototype/demo with a visible warning, and name an owner and decision date for Q1.

findings.title: No resource limits or abuse controls
findings.detail: Body is capped at 2000 chars by validation, but there is no HTTP request-size cap (node:http reads unbounded streams), no per-user note count cap, no rate limit. A2 says a few hundred notes but nothing enforces it; memory can be exhausted (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Acceptance Criteria, #Assumptions).
findings.recommendation: Add requirements and ACs: max request payload (413 above N KB), max notes per user with a defined error, and state rate limiting is gateway-owned. Add tests.

findings.title: Identity header handling underspecified
findings.detail: AC6 covers only a missing X-User. Empty, whitespace, overlong, odd-character values and repeated headers are unspecified; a value like '__proto__' could break a plain-object store. Safety relies solely on README text for A1 (RISK-1) (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Risks).
findings.recommendation: Define X-User validation (charset/length, 401 otherwise), require Map-based storage, add a test. Add a technical control for A1 (e.g. loopback/configurable bind host) beyond documentation.

findings.title: Validation and error contract gaps
findings.detail: AC5 does not define behaviour for non-string or missing title/body, non-object JSON, wrong content-type, unknown routes, wrong methods, invalid id format, or check order (401 before parse). 'Never causes a server error' needs a generic 500 policy that leaks nothing.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate these cases in AC5 with status codes; require a generic 500 body without stack traces, tested.

findings.title: Risk register incomplete
findings.detail: Risks lack likelihood, impact and owner; missing: header spoofing via gateway misconfiguration, memory exhaustion, id guessability.
findings.recommendation: Convert to a table with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner and add the missing risks.

findings.title: Unspecified note schema, ids, ordering, logging
findings.detail: No id format, list ordering, timestamps, response shape for 'stored note', or logging policy is defined.
findings.recommendation: Specify note schema (UUID id, owner, title, body, createdAt), list ordering, and minimal request logging that excludes bodies.

findings.recommendation: State a total-store cap or explicitly rely on the gateway in the README.
